# OpenUI ToolPkg

OpenUI is an optional external plugin. Install and enable **OpenUI** from the plugin catalog to use it. It is disabled by default and contributes no model instructions while disabled.

The plugin uses the unmodified official packages from Thesys's thesysdev/openui repository:

- @openuidev/react-lang 1.0.2: the OpenUI Lang parser, reactive runtime and Renderer.
- @openuidev/react-ui 0.18.1: the complete openuiLibrary, official components, theme provider and stylesheet.

The lockfile pins the dependency graph. The package does not implement its own OpenUI grammar or replace the upstream widgets. dist/upstream.json records every component shipped by that exact library. The system prompt is generated by that same library during packaging.

## Message protocol

Write an explicit plugin XML block on separate lines:

~~~text
<openui>
root = Card([TextContent("Hello from OpenUI")])
</openui>
~~~

Only the XML envelope belongs to this plugin. The body is passed verbatim to the official renderer. The closing tag is reserved and must not occur inside a program string. Open blocks use the upstream streaming mode; a closing tag enables interactions. Ordinary Markdown and LaTeX use their existing renderers. There is no OpenUI message enum, OpenUI string detection, or OpenUI renderer in Rust or Flutter.

## Ownership

- ToolPkg.registerXmlRenderPlugin handles the openui tag through the existing generic XML channel.
- ToolPkg.registerSystemPromptComposeHook supplies the exact library-generated instructions while this plugin is enabled.
- One React root and WebView survive stream updates; upstream reactive and form state remain in that instance. The Compose screen retains form state across browser-document recreation during that screen's lifetime.
- Query and Mutation call the normal host tool interface. No direct platform filesystem or HTTP implementation is added.
- Continue-conversation actions send the original action object, including form values, to the owning chat using Chat.sendMessage.
- URL actions open a separate plugin browser dialog. That browser never receives the renderer's privileged JavaScript interface.
- Package scripts and styles are served offline by the existing resource host. Remote component resources, such as image URLs, retain their HTTP/HTTPS behavior.
- Effective light/dark mode comes from the host theme service and is applied through the official ThemeProvider.

## Development

Run inside this package:

~~~sh
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm run check
corepack pnpm exec playwright install chromium
corepack pnpm test
corepack pnpm run pack:toolpkg
~~~

Packaging writes dist/openui.toolpkg and the matching core/crates/runtime/application/assets/plugins/external/openui.toolpkg in the same worktree. It does not build Rust or Flutter or deliver anything to a running application. The archive includes editable source files and upstream license notices.
